transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And thank you to the people of Hartford, our hosts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to begin by saying again how much I respect Senator Dole and his record of public service and how hard I will try to make this campaign and this debate one of ideas, not insults.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Four years ago I ran for president at a time of high unemployment and rising frustration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I wanted to turn this country around with a program of opportunity for all, responsibility from all, and an American community where everybody has a role to play.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I wanted a government that was smaller and less bureaucratic to help people make the most of their own lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Four years ago you took me on faith.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now there’s a record: Ten and a half million more jobs, rising incomes, falling crime rates and welfare rolls, a strong America at peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We are better off than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s keep it going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We cut the deficit by 60 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, let’s balance the budget and protect Medicare, Medicaid, education and the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We cut taxes for 15 million working Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now let’s pass the tax cuts for education and child rearing, help with medical emergencies, and buying a home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We passed family and medical leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now let’s expand it so more people can succeed as parents and in the work force.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We passed 100,000 police, the assault weapons ban, the Brady Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now let’s keep going by finishing the work of putting the police on the street and tackling juvenile gangs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We passed welfare reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now let’s move a million people from welfare to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And most important, let’s make education our highest priority so that every eight-year-old will be able to read, every 12-year-old can log onto the Internet, every 18-year-old can go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can build that bridge to the 21st Century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I look forward to discussing exactly how we’re going to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, for those kind words.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank the people of Hartford, the Commission, and all those out here who may be listening or watching.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a great honor for me to be here standing here as the Republican nominee.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m very proud to be the Republican nominee reaching out to Democrats and Independents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have three very special people with me tonight: My wife, Elizabeth; my daughter, Robin, who has never let me down, and a fellow named Frank Carafa from New York, along with Ollie Manninen who helped me out in the mountains of Italy a few years back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve learned from them that people do have tough times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And sometimes you can’t go it alone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what America is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I remember getting my future back from doctors and nurses and a doctor in Chicago named Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Kalikian .

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And ever since that time, I’ve tried to give something back to my country, to the people who are watching us tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: America is the greatest place on the face of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, I know millions of you still have anxieties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You work harder and harder to make ends meet and put food on the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You worry about the quality and the safety of your children, and the quality of education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But even more importantly, you worry about the future and will they have the same opportunities that you and I have had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And Jack Kemp and I want to share with you some ideas tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Jack Kemp is my running mate, doing an outstanding job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’m a plain-speaking man and I learned long ago that your word was your bond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I promise you tonight that I’ll try to address your concerns and not try to exploit them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a tall order, but I’ve been running against the odds for a long time and, again, I’m honored to be here this evening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, I believe that the Federal government should give people the tools and try to establish the conditions in which they can make the most of their own lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That, to me, is the key.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that leads me to some different conclusions from Senator Dole.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: For example, we have reduced the size of the Federal government to its smallest size in 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We reduced more regulations, eliminated more programs than my two Republican predecessors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I have worked hard for things like the Family and Medical Leave Law, the Brady Bill, the assault weapons ban, the program to put 100,000 police on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: All of these are programs that Senator Dole opposed that I supported, because I felt they were a legitimate effort to help people make the most of their own lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked hard to help families impart values to their own children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I supported the V-chip so that parents would be able to control what their kids watch on television when they’re young, along with the ratings systems for television and educational television.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I supported strong action against the tobacco companies to stop the marketing, advertising, and sale of tobacco to young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I supported a big increase in the safe and drug-free schools program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: These were areas on which Senator Dole and I differed, but I believed they were the right areas for America to be acting together as one country to help individuals and families make the most of their own lives and raise their kids with good values and a good future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think the basic difference is, and I have had some experience in this, I think the basic difference, I trust the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President trusts the government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We go back and look at the healthcare plan that he wanted to impose on the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: One seventh the total economy, 17 new taxes, price controls, 35 to 50 new bureaucracies that cost $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 5 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Don’t forget that, that happened in 1993.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: A tax increase, a tax on everybody in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Not just the rich.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you made 25,000 as the original proposal, you got your Social Security taxes increased.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had a BTU tax we turned into a $35 million gas tax, a $265 billion tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I guess I rely more on the individual.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I carry a little card in my pocket called the Tenth Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Where possible, I want to give power back to the states and back to the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s my difference with the President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ll have specific differences later.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He noted a few, but there are others.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I trust the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done a lot to give the people more powers to make their own decisions over their own lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I do think we are right when we try to, for example, give mothers and newborns 48 hours before they can be kicked out of the hospital, ending these drive-by deliveries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we were right to pass the Kassebaum-Kennedy bill, which says you can’t lose your health insurance just because you change jobs or because someone in your family’s been sick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our government is smaller and less bureaucratic and has given more authority to the states than its two predecessors under Republican presidents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I do believe we have to help our people get ready to succeed in the 21st Century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, he’s better off than he was four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I may be better off four years from now, but I don’t know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I looked at the slowest growth in the century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He inherited a growth of 4.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 8 percent, now it’s down to about 2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 4 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to pass a million bankruptcies this year for the first time in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got stagnant wages.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In fact, women’s wages have dropped 2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 2 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Men’s wages haven’t gone up, gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we have stagnation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have the highest foreign debt in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it seems to me that if you take a look, are you better off?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I guess some may be better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Saddam Hussein is probably better off than he was four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Renee Proval is probably better off than he was four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But are the American people?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re working harder and higher and harder paying more taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: For the first time in history, you pay about 40 percent of what you earn.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: More than you spend for food, clothing and shelter combined for taxes under this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So some may be better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They talk about family income being up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true in Connecticut, family income is down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it’s up in some cases because both parents are working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: One works for the family, and one works to pay taxes for the government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to give them tax cuts so they can spend more time with their children, maybe even take a vacation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s what America is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me say, first of all, in February Senator Dole acknowledged that the American economy was in the best shape it’s been in in 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have ten and a half million more jobs, a faster job growth rate than under any Republican administration since the 1920s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wages are goings up for the first time in a decade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have record numbers of new small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have the biggest drop in the number of people in poverty in 27 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: All groups of people are growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We had the biggest drop in income inequality in 27 years in 1995.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The average family’s income has gone up over $1600 just since our economic plan passed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think it’s clear that we’re better off than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now we need to focus on what do we need to do to be better off still.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: How can we help people as we are to get their retirements when they work for small businesses, to be able to afford health insurance, to be able to educate their children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I want to focus on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we are clearly better off than we were four years ago, as Senator Dole acknowledged this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I doubt that I acknowledged that this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But in any event, I think we just look at the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ask the people that are viewing tonight, are you better off than you were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s not whether we’re better off, it’s whether they’re better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Are you working harder to put food on the table, feed your children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Are your children getting a better education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Drug use has doubled the past 44 months all across America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Crime has gone down but it’s because the mayors like Rudy Giuliani where one third of the drop happened in one city, New York City.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So, yes, some may be better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But of the people listening tonight, the working families who will benefit from economic packages, they’ll be better off when Bob Dole is president and Jack Kemp is vice president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s look at the position.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, remember that in this campaign season, since Senator Dole’s been a candidate, he has bragged about the fact that he voted against Medicare in the beginning, in 1965, one of only 12 members.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said he did the right thing then, he knew it wouldn’t work at the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what he said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then his budget that he passed along with Speaker Gingrich cut Medicare $270 billion, more than was necessary to repair the Medicare trust fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It would have charged seniors more for out-of-pocket costs as well as more in premiums because doctors could have charged them more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The American Medical, Hospital Association, the Nurses Association, the Catholic Hospital Association all said hundreds of hospitals could close and people would be hurt badly under the Dole-Gingrich Medicare plan that I vetoed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And now with this risky $550 billion tax scheme of Senator Dole’s, even his own friends, his campaign co-chair, Senator D’Amato, says that they can’t possibly pay for it without cutting Medicare more and cutting Social Security as well, according to him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, my balanced budget plan adds ten years to the life of the Medicare trust fund, ten years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll have time to deal with the long-term problems of the baby boomers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it was simply wrong to finance their last scheme to cut Medicare $270 billion to run the risk of it withering on the vine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We always had to reform it over the years, but we need somebody who believes it in to reform it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I must say, I look back at the vote on Medicare in 1965, we had a program called Eldercare that also provided drugs and means tests to people who needed medical attention received it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I thought it was a good program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I’ve supported Medicare ever since.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In fact, I used to go home, my mother would tell me, Bob, all I’ve got is my Social Security and my Medicare, don’t cut it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t violate anything my mother said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In fact, we had a conversation about our mothers one day, a very poignant conversation in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m concerned about healthcare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve had the best healthcare from government hospitals, Army hospitals and I know its importance, but we’ve got to fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s his trustees, the President’s trustees, not mine, who says it’s going to go broke.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He doesn’t fix it for ten years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to appoint a commission, just as we did in Social Security in 1983, when we rescued Social Security, and I was proud to be on that commission, along with Claude Pepper, the champion of senior citizens from Florida.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And we can do it again, if we take politics out of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Stop scaring the seniors, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’ve already spent $45 million scaring seniors and tearing me apart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s time to have a truce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me say, first of all, I’d be happy to have a commission deal with this and I appreciate what Senator Dole did on the ’83 Social Security commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it won’t be possible to do, if his tax scheme passes because even his own campaign co-chair, Senator D’Amato, says he’ll have to cut Medicare even more than was cut in the bill that I vetoed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I vetoed that bill because it cut more Medicare and and basically ran the risk of breaking up the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My balanced budget plan puts ten years on the Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We ought to do that, then we can have a commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But Senator Dole’s plans are not good for the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Oh, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And you’ll be eligible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Me too?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And so will the former President, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I need it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, the people need it, that’s the point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is not a Wall Street tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is a family tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is a Main Street tax cut, 15 percent across — let’s take a family making $30,000 a year, that’s $1261.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, maybe to some in this Bushnell Memorial that it’s not a lot of money, but people watching tonight with a couple of kids, a working family, that’s four or five months of day care, maybe a personal computer; it’s may be three or four months of mortgage payments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This economic package is about families but it’s a six-point package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: First of all, it’s a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution which President Clinton defeated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He twisted arms and got six Democrats to vote the other way, but we lost by one vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s balancing a budget by the year 2002.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a tax cut, cutting capital gains 50 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So you can go out and create more jobs and more opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a state tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a $500 per child tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about litigation reforms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now that the President gets millions of dollars from the trial lawyers, he probably doesn’t like this provision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In fact, when I fell off the podium in Chico, before I lit the ground, hit the ground I had call on my cell phone from a trial lawyer saying I think we’ve got a case here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it’s also regulatory reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a good package, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’d like to have your support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, here’s the problem with it: It sounds very good, but there’s a reason that 500 economists, including seven Nobel prize winners and business periodicals like Business Week, and even Senator Dole’s friends, Senator Warren Rudman, former Republican senator from New Hampshire, says it’s not a practical program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s a $550 billion tax scheme that will cause a big hole in the deficit which will raise interest rates and slow down the economy and cause people to pay more for home mortgages, car payments, credit card payments, college loans, and small business loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s not good to raise the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We worked too hard to lower it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It will actually raise taxes on nine million people and, in addition to that, it will force bigger cuts in Medicare, Medicaid, education and the environment than the ones that he and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Gingrich passed that I vetoed last year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So it sounds great, but our targeted tax cut for education, child rearing, healthcare and home buying, which is paid for in my balanced budget plan, something that he has not done, certified by the Congressional budget office, that’s the right way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President wants to increase spending 20 percent over the next six years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to increase spending 14 percent, that’s how simple it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want the government to pinch pennies for a change instead of the American families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re talking about six percentage points over six years, and with that money you give it back to the working people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You also provide opportunity scholarships so low income parents will have the same choice that others have in sending their children to better schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It will work, and when it does work, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, I know you’ll congratulate me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I try to articulate my positions as clearly as possible, tell people what I stand for and let them decide whether they’re going to support me or not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Senator mentioned the trial lawyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In the case of the product liability bill, which they passed and I vetoed, I think that’s what he’s talking about, I actually wanted to sign that bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I told the people exactly what the Congress exactly what kind of bill I would sign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, a lot of the trial lawyers didn’t want me to sign any bill at all, but I had thought we ought to do what we could to cut frivolous lawsuits, but they wouldn’t make some of the changes that I thought should be made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me just give you an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I had a person in the Oval Office who lost a child in a school bus accident where a drunk driver caused the accident directly, but there were problems with the school bus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The drunk driver had no money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Under the new bill, if I had signed it, a person like that could never have had any recovery.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I thought that was wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I gave four or five specific examples to the Congress and said, prove to me that these people could recover but we’re going to eliminate frivolous lawsuits, I’ll sign the bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But generally I believe that a president has to be willing to do what he thinks is right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve done a lot of things that were controversial.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My economic plan, my trade position, Bosnia, Haiti, taking on the NRA for the first time, taking on the tobacco companies for the first time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes you just have to do that because you know it’s right for the country over the long run.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’ve tried to do and that’s what I will continue to do as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: How does he avoid conflict?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t know in the case of the trial lawyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I look at the trial lawyers, and when you’re a few million short, you run out to Hollywood and pick up two to four million and organized labor comes to Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: and puts 35 million into the pot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, if these aren’t special interests, I’ve got a lot to learn.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I was there for a while before I left on June the 11th.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The trial lawyers and I don’t — you know, my wife’s a lawyer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re the only two lawyers in Washington that trust each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But we’re lawyers, I like lawyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t dislike trial lawyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it seemed to me there’s got to be some end to the frivolous lawsuits and there’s got to be some cap on punitive damage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re putting a lot of business people out of business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Small businessmen and businesswomen who paid 70 percent of your ninteen , your$265 billion tax increase, the largest tax increase in the history of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I said that one day and Pat Moynihan, a Democrat, say, no, he said, in the history of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I modified it, the largest tax increase in the history of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it seems to me that there is a problem there, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I will address you as Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You didn’t do that with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: with President Bush in 1992.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say, first of all, I signed a tort reform bill that dealt with civilian aviation a couple of years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I proved that I will sign reasonable tort reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, Senator Dole had some pretty harsh comments about special interest money, but it wasn’t me who opposed what we tried to do to save the lives of children who were subject to tobacco and then went to the tobacco growers and bragged about standing up for the Federal government when we tried to stop the advertising, marketing, and sales of tobacco to children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it wasn’t me that let the polluters actually come into the halls of Congress, into the rooms, and rewrite the environmental laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what Speaker Gingrich and Senator Dole did, not me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I believe that we should take a different approach to this and talk about how we stand on the issues instead of trying to characterize each other’s motivations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think Senator Dole and I just honestly disagree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s very difficult.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s be honest about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we need campaign finance reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I reach out to the Perot voters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done about all, we are the reform party, the Republican Party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And the Perot voters that are looking for a home ought to take a look at the Republican record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Whatever it is, whatever the checklist was in ’92, it’s all done with campaign finance reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I worked with Senator Mitchell, who played me, I guess, in the debate warmup.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We tried six or eight years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He appointed three people, I appointed three people to get campaign finance reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We couldn’t get it done, because I wasn’t enforceable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’ve suggested a commission, Newt Gingrich did, I suggested that at least four or five years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have a commission on campaign finance reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They send it to Congress, and we have to vote it up or down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s how it works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We are never going to fix it by the parties, because Democrats want a better advantage for themselves, we want a better advantage as Republicans, and that’s not how it’s going to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I want to touch on this is tobacco thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know the President’s been puffing a lot on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I want to go back to 1965.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That was my first vote against tobacco companies when I said we ought to label cigarettes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve had a consistent record ever since 1965.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We passed a bill in 1992 that encouraged the states to adopt programs to stop kids from smoking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: All 50 states did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It took three and a half years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It wasn’t until election year, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, that you ever thought about stopping smoking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What about drugs that have increased, doubled in the last 44 months?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Cocaine is up 141 percent — marijuana, cocaine up 166 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It seems to me that you have a selective memory.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, mine doesn’t work that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I just want to try to correct it as we go along.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Lehrer, I hope we’ll have a chance to discuss drugs later in the program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let me respond to what you said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree that too many incumbent politicians in Washington in both parties have consistently opposed campaign finance reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That was certainly the case from the minute I got there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So after Speaker Gingrich and Senator Dole took over the Congress, I went to New Hampshire and a man suggested — a gentleman that unfortunately just passed away a couple of days ago, suggested that we appoint a commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I shook hands with him on it and I appointed my members, and the commission never met.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And then Senator Dole’s ardent supporters, Senator McCain, who’s out there today, along with Senator Feingold, supported, sponsored a campaign finance reform proposal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I strongly supported it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And members of Senator Dole’s own party in the Senate killed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And he was not out there urging them to vote for the McCain-Feingold bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think the American people, including the Perot supporters, know that I have had a consistent record in favor of campaign finance reform, and I will continue to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I hope we can finally get it in the next session of Congress, because we need it badly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, on campaign reform itself, we’re going to get it when we have a bipartisan commission, take it out of politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Get people who don’t have any interest in politics but understand the issue and let them make the recommendation to Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’re now kidding anybody, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: These are sophisticated people watching tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Millions and millions of Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They know the Republican Party hasn’t done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They know the Democratic party won’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to agree that somebody else should do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And we have to vote it up or down, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, I think every American in any position of responsibility should be concerned about what’s happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let’s look at the overall record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Overall in America cocaine use has dropped 30 percent in the last four years, casual drug use down 13 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The tragedy is that our young people are still increasing their use of drugs up to about 11 percent total with marijuana, and I regret it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you what I tried to do about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I appointed a four-star general who led our efforts south of the border to keep drugs from coming into the country as our nation’s drug czar.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The most heavily directed, decorated solder in uniform when he retired.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We submitted the biggest drug budget ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have dramatically increased control and enforcement at the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We supported a a crime bill that had 60 death penalties including, including the death penalty for drug kingpins.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I supported a big expansion in safe and drug-free schools program to support things like the DARE program because I thought all those things were very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Do I think that I bear some responsibility for the fact that too many of our children still don’t understand drugs are wrong, drugs can kill you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Even though I have consistently opposed the legalization of drugs all my public life and worked hard against them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we all do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I hope we can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think this issue should be politicized because my record is clear and I don’t think Senator Dole supports using using drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we just have to continue to work on this until those who think it isn’t dangerous and won’t kill them and won’t destroy their lives, get the message and change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Again, well it’s, you are very selective, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You don’t want to politicize drugs, but it’s already politicized Medicare, go out and scare senior citizens and other vulnerable groups, veterans and people who get Pell Grants and things like this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you say we’ve done all these bad things, which isn’t the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it seems to me the record is clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The record is pretty clear in Arkansas, when you were governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Drug use doubled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You resisted the appointment of a drug czar there because you thought it might interfere with treatment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But here you cut the drug czar’s office 83 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You cut interdiction substantially.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean that’s what, I want to stop it from coming across the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And in my administration, we’re going to train the National Guard to stop it from coming across the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is a invasion of drugs from all over the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And we have a responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You had a surgeon — or before General McCaffrey you had a lady who said we ought to consider legalizing drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Is that the kind of leadership we need?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I won’t comment on other things that happened in your administration or your past about drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it seems to me the kids ought to — if they’ve started, they ought to stop and just don’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say again, we did have a drug czar in Arkansas, but he answered to the governor, just like this one answers to the President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I thought we ought to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, Senator Dole, you voted against the crime bill that had the death penalty for drug kingpins in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you voted to cut services to 23 million school children under the safe and drug-free schools act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that means you’re soft on drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just have a different approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let me remind you, my family has suffered from drug abuse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like to see somebody you love nearly lose their lives, and I hate drugs, Senator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to do this together and we can.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Not if I didn’t have a better idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I’ve got a better idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s something I’ve worked on for 15 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s called the automated check or the instant check.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s being used in 17 states right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: States like Florida, Colorado, Virginia, and other states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You don’t buy any gun.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You don’t get any gun.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got 20 million names on a computer in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: of people who should not have guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to keep guns out of the hands of criminals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And, there are eight other categories that should not have guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been working on this for a long, long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You walk in, you put your little card in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If it says tilt, you don’t get any gun.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You don’t get a hand gun, you don’t get a rifle, you don’t get a shot gun, you get zippo.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If we’re going to protect American children and American families and people who live as prisoners in their own home, we’ve got to stop guns from being dumped on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The administration says they support the instant check.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’ve appropriated about $200 million, but only spent about $3 million to get it underway.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In our administration, in my administration, we will expedite.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This keeps up with technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It keeps guns out of the hands of people who should not have guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That is the bottom line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I believe it’s a good idea, has strong bipartisan support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And perhaps that’s another thing we can depoliticize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You talk about the Brady Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There has only been one prosecution under the Brady — only one under the assault weapon ban and only seven under the Brady Bill that you talk about all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And on the assault weapon ban, out of 17 weapons that were banned, only six banned now because eleven have been modified and are back on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s get together on this instant check because that will really make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say, first of all, Senator Dole has gone back and forth about whether he’d be for repealing the Brady Bill or repealing the assault weapons ban.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think his present position is he would not do so, and if that’s true I’m grateful for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let’s look at the facts here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Brady Bill has kept at least 60,000 felons, fugitives and stalkers from getting hand guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole led the fight against the Brady Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He tried to keep it from coming to my desk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t succeed and I signed it and I’m glad I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then when we had the assault weapons ban in the Senate, Senator Dole fought it bitterly and opposed the entire crime bill and almost brought the entire crime bill down because the National Rifle Association didn’t want the assault weapons ban, just like they didn’t want the Brady Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But two years later nobody’s lost their handguns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I mean, their rifles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve expanded the Brady Bill to cover people who beat up their spouses and their kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And this is a safer country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I’m glad I took on that fight and I believe, with all respect, I was right and he was wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, the President doesn’t have it quite right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean, it seemed to me at the time the assault weapon ban was not effective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But that’s history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I told the NRA that’s history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re not going to worry about it anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to worry about it anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s do something better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s stop, you know, playing the political game, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Talking about this and this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You add all the states that’ve used the instant check and how many weapons they keep, kept out of the hands of criminals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It would far surpass the numbers you mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So in my view, if you want to be protected, you ought to vote for Bob Dole and we’ll get the instant check passed and we’ll keep guns out of the hands of criminals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If he, that’s what he said, he’s not right about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look at where we are today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The United States is still the indispensable nation in the aftermath of the Cold War and on the brink of the 21st Century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have worked to support our country as the world’s strongest force for peace and freedom, prosperity and security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have done the following things: Number one, we’ve managed the aftermath of the Cold War, supporting a big drop in nuclear weapons in Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The removal of Russian troops from the Baltics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The integration of Central and Eastern European democracies into a new partnership with NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, I might add, with the democratic Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are no nuclear missiles pointed at the children of the United States tonight and have not been in our administration for the first time since the dawn of the nuclear age.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have worked hard for peace and freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I took office, Haiti was governed by a dictator that had defied the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I took office, the worst war in Europe was waging in Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now there is a the democratically elected president in Haiti.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Peace in Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just had the election there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve made progress in Northern Ireland, in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve also stood up to the new threats of terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, organized crime, and we have worked hard to expand America’s economic presence around the world with the biggest increase in trade with the largest new number of trade agreements in history And that’s one of the reasons America is number one in auto production again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I have a different view.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Again, Iâ€™ve supported the President on Bosnia, and I think we were told the troops would be out in a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now I understand it’s been extended ’til some time next year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But, let’s start with Somalia, where they dragged Americans through the streets, and where 18 Americans were killed one day, because they didn’t have, they were pinned down for eight hours, the rangers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They didn’t have the weapons, they didn’t have the tanks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They asked for the tanks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They didn’t get the tanks from this administration because we were nation building.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s called mission creep.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We turn it over to the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President didn’t have much to do about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You look at Haiti, where we spend about three billion dollars and we got an alarm call there about two weeks ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You got to send down some more people, because the president’s found out there are death squads on his on his, in his own property.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we need more protection from America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Bosnia, Northern Ireland.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There’s no ceasefire in Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think there are still lot of problems in Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We agreed to train and arm the Muslims so they could defend themselves, the policy you had when you ran in 1992.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t done that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re way behind, which means Americans can’t come home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Americans shouldn’t have gone there in the first place, had we let them defend themselves, as they have a right to do under Article 57 of the United Nations charter.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I take full responsibility for what happened in Somalia, but the American people must remember that those soldiers were under an American commander when that happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe they did the best they could under the circumstances, and let’s not forget that hundreds of thousands of lives were saved there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, in Haiti, political violence is much, much smaller than it was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thirdly, in Bosnia it’s a virtual miracle that there has been no return to war and at least there has now been an election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And institutions are beginning to function.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In Northern Ireland, in the Middle East we are better off than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There will always be problems in this whole world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But if we’re moving in the right direction and America is leading, we’re better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well it, after World War I, we had, you know, a policy of disengagement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Then from World War I to World War II we had sort of a compulsory engagement policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now I think we have a selective engagement policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have to determine when our interests are involved, not the United Nations’ interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And many of the things the President talked about, he turned over to the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They decided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He’s deployed more troops than any president in history around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s cost us billions and billions of dollars for peace-keeping operations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Look these are facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it seems to me that when you make a decision, the decision is made by the President of the United States, by the Commander-in-Chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He makes that decision when he commits young men or young women who are going to go round and defend our liberty and our freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That would be my position.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Then I’m going to have a top down review at the Pentagon, not a bottom up review.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We all fight over how much money is there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want a top down review to determine what our priorities are and what we should do in defense, and then follow that policy instead of this bottom up review with all the services fighting for the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, the President said he was going to cut defense $60 billion, he cut defense $112 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Devastated states like California and others.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think now we’ve got a problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to go back and look.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s just like you said in Texas one day, you know raised taxes too much, and you did, and you cut defense too much, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, and you did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You may have said that, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But the bottom line is, we are the strongest nation in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We provide the leadership and we’re going to have to continue to provide the leadership, but let’s do it on our terms when our interests are involved and not when somebody blows the whistle at the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our military is the strongest military in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is the strongest, best prepared, best equipped it has ever been.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There is very little difference in the budget that I proposed and the Republican budget over the next six-year period.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We are spending a lot of money to modernize our weapons system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have proposed a lot of new investments to improve the quality of life for our soldiers, for our men and women in uniform, for their families, for their training.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is my solemn obligation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You ask when do you decide to deploy them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The interests of the American people must be at stake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our values must be at stake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to be able to make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And frankly we have to consider what the risks are to our young men and women in uniform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I believe the evidence is that our deployments have been successful, in Haiti, in Bosnia, when we moved to Kuwait to repel Saddam Hussein’s threatened invasion of Kuwait.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I have sent the fleet into the Taiwan straits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When we’ve worked hard to end the Northern Korean nuclear threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe the United States is at peace tonight in part because of the disciplined, careful, effective deployment of our military resources.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well I failed to mention North Korea and Cuba, a while ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You look at North Korea where they have enough plutonium to build six nuclear bombs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve sort of distanced ourselves from our ally, South Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They lost about a million people in the war, the Korean War, the forgotten war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We lost 53,000 Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We shouldn’t be doing any favors for North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a closed society.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have any inspection.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know whether it’s going to work or not, but we keep giving the incentives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Someone called them something else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Incentives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know what’s going to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Here we have Cuba 90 miles from our shores, and what have we done, we passed the law that gave people a right to sue and the President postponed it for six months.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it seemed to me if you want to send a signal, you’ve got to send a signal, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The sooner the better off we’ll be, if you put tougher sanctions on Castro, not try to make it easier for him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, for the last four years we have worked had to put more and more pressure on the Castro government to bring about more openness and move toward democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In 1992, before I became President, the Congress passed the Cuba Democracy Act and I enforced it vigorously.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We made the embargo tougher but we increased contacts people to people with the Cubans, including direct telephone service, which was largely supported by the Cuban-American community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then Cuba shot down two of our planes and murdered four people in international air space.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They were completely beyond the pale of the law, and I signed the Helms-Burton legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole is correct.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I did give about six months before the effective date of the act before lawsuits can actually be filed, even though they’re effective now, and can be legally binding, because I want to change Cuba.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the United States needs help from other countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Nobody in the world agrees with our policy on Cuba now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But this law can be used as leverage to get other countries to help us to move Cuba to democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Every single country in Latin America, Central America and the Caribbean is a democracy tonight but Cuba.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And if we stay firm and strong, we will be able to bring Cuba around as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s the point I made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have to be firm and strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I hope that will happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It will happen starting next January and maybe it can happen the balance of this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have not been firm and strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You look at the poor people who still live in Cuba.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a haven for drug smugglers and we don’t have a firm policy when it comes to Fidel Castro.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In my view, the policy has failed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So Congress passes the law, the President signs it, like he does a lot of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But he, like welfare reform, I’m going to sign it but I’m going to try to change it next year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: A lot of these election-year conversions, the President talks about the drug money, and all the other things, all this antismoking campaign all happened in 1996.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think the people viewing out there ought to go back and take a look at the record when he fought a balanced budget amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When he gave you that biggest tax increase in history; when he tried to take over your healthcare system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When he fought regulatory reform that cost the average family 6 to $7,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is a serious business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about your family; it’s about your business, and in this case it’s about a firmer policy with Cuba.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There were several off-the-subject quaffers in that litany.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me just mention, Senator Dole voted for $900 billion in tax increases.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: His running mate Jack Kemp once said that Bob Dole never met a tax he didn’t hike.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And everybody knows, including the Wall Street Journal, hardly a friend of the Democratic party of this administration, that the ’82 tax increase he sponsored in inflation-adjusted dollars was the biggest tax increase in American history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we ought to at least get the facts out here on the table so we can know where to go from here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let me first answer that question about the 1982 tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We were closing loopholes, we were going after big corporations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know you probably would oppose it, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, but I think we should have a fairer system and a flatter system, and we’ll have a fairer and flatter system and we’re going to make the economic package work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Healthcare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, we finally passed the Kassebaum bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President was opposed to it in 1993.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He wanted to give us this big system, that took over about one-seventh of the economy, that put on price controls, created all these state alliances, and would cost $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 5 trillion and force people into managed care, whether they wanted it or not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Most people want to see their own doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re going to see their own doctor when Bob Dole is president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We won’t threaten anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we passed the Kassebaum-Kennedy, the Kennedy Kassebaum bill that will cover about 20 to 25 million people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been for that for four, five, six years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President held it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And even when it finally got near passage, Senator Kennedy held it up for 100 days, because he wasn’t satisfied with one provision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it will cover preexisting conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you change your job, you’re going to be covered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So there are a lot of good things in this bill we should have done instead of trying this massive, massive takeover by the Federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But then of course we had a Democratic Congress and they didn’t want to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Until we got a Republican Congress, we finally got action, I’m proud of my colleagues in the Republican Party for getting that done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It means a lot to a lot of people watching us tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, that sounds very good, but it’s very wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole remembers well that we actually offered not to even put in a healthcare bill in 1994, uh ’93, but instead to work with the Senate Republicans and write a joint bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And they said no because they got a memo from one of their political advisers saying that instead they should characterize whatever we did as big government and make sure nothing was done to aid healthcare before the ’94 elections so they could make that claim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, maybe we bit off more than we could chew, but we’re pursuing a step-by-step reform now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Kennedy-Kassebaum bill that I signed will make it possible for 25 million people to keep their health insurance when they change jobs or when somebody in their family’s been sick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I signed a bill to stop these drive-by deliveries when insurance companies can force people out of the hospital after 24 hours and I vetoed Senator Dole’s Medicare plan that would have forced a lot of seniors into managed care and taken a lot more money out of their pockets and led to Medicare withering on the vine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, many of the provisions in the Kassebaum bill were provisions that — my provisions, like deductions for long-term care, making certain that self-employed people that are watching tonight can deduct not 30 percent but 80 percent of you pay for premiums.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You can also deduct long-term care now, so it’s a good it’s a good start.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think there’s enough — we’re even looking at our tax cut proposal, our economic package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
