transcript_turns.text: There may be a way of reaching out to the uninsured, because there are a lot of uninsured people in the country, particularly children, that should be covered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Another way you can do is to expand Medicaid.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In America no one will go without healthcare, no one will go without food.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: All right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Food.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, the president’s own CIA director says Saddam is stronger now than he was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t understand extending the no-fly zone in the south when the trouble was in the north.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And what we’ve done during the Bush administration, the Kurds were at the State Department, negotiating, trying to work their differences out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now we’ve got all thousands and thousands of refugees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re even shipping 3,000 Kurds to Guam.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It involves Turkey.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a real problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Saddam is probably about as strong as he ever was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We shot, what, 44 cruise missiles, worth about a million-two a piece, and hit some radar, that repaired in a couple, three days.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Did we inflict any damage?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Did we have any allies helping?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, we have Great Britain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re always very loyal to us, and I appreciate that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And of course Kuwait.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Even though they had to find out they had 5,000 troops coming, they didn’t even understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had to get their permission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The bottom line is, we went in there alone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We are supposed to be operating under a U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: resolution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We did it without any of our allies that helped in the Gulf.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole has two or three times before tonight criticized me for working with the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now I’m being criticized for not working with the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s not the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes the United States has to act alone or at least has to act first.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes we cannot let other countries have a veto on our foreign policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I could not send soldiers into the north of Iraq, that would have been wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It could reduce Saddam Hussein’s abilities to threaten Kuwait and his other neighbors again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I still believe it was the right thing to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Not mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, there were some good pictures, but does it fall into that category?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to be very serious.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve supported the President when I thought he was right on Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I supported him on NAFTA and GATT.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So it’s not that we always disagree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Others disagreed with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The Mideast is very difficult.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it seemed to me just as an observer that you know before you’d call somebody to America, you’d have some notion what the end result might be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now maybe it’s better just to get together and sit down and talk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe that was the purpose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I know talks have started again today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But again it’s almost like an ad hoc foreign policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s ad hoc, it’s sort of we get up in the morning and read the papers, what country’s in trouble, we’ll have a meeting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, to me that’s not the strategy that I think people expect from America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think we have lost credibility, and I say this very honestly without any partisanship.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve lost credibility around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Our allies know, — they’re not certain what we’re going to do, what our reaction, what our response is going to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Nobody suggested sending troops to Iraq, if that was the hint there from the President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I do think that Saddam Hussein is stronger than he was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I do believe that we didn’t gain a great deal in the Mideast by bringing three of the four leaders, one refused to come, to Washington D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have a very consistent policy in the Middle East: It is to support the peace process; to support the security of Israel; and to support those who are prepared to take risks for peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is a very difficult environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The feelings are very strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are extremists in all parts of the Middle East who want to kill that peace process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Prime Minister Rabin gave his life because someone in his own country literally hated him for trying to bring peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would like to have had a big, organized summit, but those people were killing each other, rapidly, innocent Arab children, innocent Israeli people, they were dying.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And there is ,so much trust has broken down in the aftermath of the change of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I felt that if I could just get the parties together to say let’s stop the violence, start talking, commit to the negotiations, that would be a plus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now today the Secretary of State is in the Middle East and they’ve started negotiations and all those leaders promised me they would not quit until they resolved the issues between them and got the peace process going forward again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I was disappointed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President has not called for an unconditional end to the violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It seemed to me the violence stopped when these leaders came to America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The killing and tragedies had taken place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it is unfortunate, it is a difficult area, no doubt about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It shouldn’t be politicized in any way by the President or by his opponent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t intend to politicize it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I hope they talked and I hope they’ve reached some result and that the killing will end.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m saying that Senator Dole said in his fine speech in San Diego that he wanted to build a bridge to the past.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think I know what he meant by that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He’s troubled, as I am, by some of the things that go on today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I believe America is the greatest country in human history because we have maintained freedom and increasing prosperity by relentlessly pushing the barriers of knowledge, the barriers of the present, always moving into the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why when I became President I was determined to kind of move beyond this whole stale debate that had gone on in Washington for too long to get this country moving again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why we’ve got a country with ten and a half million more jobs, and record numbers of new businesses, and rising incomes, and falling crime rates, and welfare roll rates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’re moving in the right direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’m trying to emphasize that what I want to do is to continue to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why my balanced budget plan will still invest and grow this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I want a tax cut for education and child rearing, but it’s got to be paid for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I want to continue the work we have done over partisan opposition, to work with communities to bring that crime rate down until our streets are all safe again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: These are my commitments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am very oriented toward the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think this election has to be geared toward the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think America’s best days are still ahead, but we’ve got to build the right bridge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, the President reminds me sometimes of my brother Kenny, who is no longer alive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But Kenny was a great talker.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And he used to tell me things that I knew were not quite accurate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we always had a rule, we divided by six.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe in your case maybe just two.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But 11 million new jobs and everything, I mean the President can’t take credit for everything that governors are doing, whether that’s happening in New York City when it comes to the murder rate and then not be responsible for the bad things that happen, whether it’s drug use or something else in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So it seems to me that we can talk about what we call Kenny, the great exaggerator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He just liked to make it sound exager, a little better, made him feel better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to bridges, I want a bridge to the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I also want a bridge to the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have to tell the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got people watching tonight and listening tonight trying to find the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And the truth is, there is a lot wrong with America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We need a strong economic package; we need a tax cut; we need the $500 child credit, and we’ll have that soon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I do not for a moment think I’m entitled to all the credit for all the good things that have happened in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But where I have moved to work with the American people to help them have the tools to make the most of their own lives, I think I should get some credit for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I also personally took responsibility tonight when Senator Dole asked me about the drug problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But, you know, I think my ideas are better for the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole voted against student loans, against Headstart, against creating the Department of Education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If he gets elected president, we’ll start the new century without anyone in the cabinet of the President representing education in our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I personally don’t think that’s the right kind of future for America, and I think we ought to take a different tack.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t favor it when it was in, started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It was a tribute after President Carter’s election to the National Education Association who send a lot of delegates to the Democratic convention, who gives 99.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 5 percent of their money, Democrat Democrats, and the President, and a lot of the teachers send their kids to private schools or better public schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So what we want to do is called opportunity scholarships.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, some say, oh, you’re a Republican, you can’t be reaching out to these people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve reached out to people all my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked on the food stamp program, proudly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And the WIC program, and the school lunch program with senators like George McGovern, Hubert Humphrey and others, to name a few of my Democratic friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m not some extremist out here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I care about people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have my own little foundation that’s raised about $10 million for the disabled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t advertise it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Just did, haven’t before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I try to do a lot of things that I think might be helpful to people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So it seems to me that we ought to take that money we can save from the Department of Education, put it into opportunity scholarships and tell little Landale Shakespeare out in Cleveland, Ohio, and tell your mother and father, you’re going to get to go to school because we’re going to match what the state puts up, and you’re going to go to the school of your choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t fault the President or the vice president for sending their children to private schools or better schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I applaud them for it, I don’t criticize them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But why shouldn’t everybody have that choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Why shouldn’t low income Americans and low middle income Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m excited about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to be a big, big opportunity for a lot of people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say first of all, I’m all for students having more choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve worked hard to expand public school choice in my balanced budget bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s funds for 3,000 new schools created by teachers and parents, sometimes by business people, called charter schools that have no rules, they’re free of bureaucracy and can only stay in existence if they perform and teach children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The ones that are out there are doing well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What I’m against is Senator Dole’s plan to take money away from all the children we now help with limited Federal funds and help far fewer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If we’re going to have a private voucher plan, that ought to be done at the local level or the state level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But Senator Dole has consistently opposed Federal help to education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He voted against student loans; he voted against my improved student loan plan; he voted against the National Service bill, against the HeadStart bill; he voted against our efforts in safe and drug-free schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He voted against these programs, he does not believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 90 percent of our kids are out there in those public schools and we need to lift their standards and move them forward with the programs like those I’ve outlined in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’d better correct the President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know what time it is, but it’s probably getting late.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to correct, the all these things I voted against, they were probably part of some big package that had a lot of pork in it or a lot of things that we shouldn’t have had and we probably voted no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve supported all the education programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve supported Headstart, I think we ought to look at it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t want anybody out there to think we’ve just been voting no, no, no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s give low income parents the same right that people of power and prestige have in America and let them go to better schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s not, let’s help, let’s turn the schools back to the teachers and back to the parents and take it away from the National Education Association.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I support school choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I support school choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have advocated expansions of public school choice alternatives and I said the creation of 3,000 new schools that we are going to help the states to finance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But if you’re going to have a private voucher plan, that ought to be determined by states in localities where they’re raising and spending most of the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I simply think it’s wrong to take money away from programs that are helping build basic skills for kids, 90 percent of them are in the public schools; to take money away from programs that are helping fund the school lunch program, that are helping to fund the other programs, that are helping our schools to improve their standards.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our schools are getting better, and our schools can be made to be even better still with the right kind of community leadership and partnership at the school level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have been a strong force for reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, Senator, I remind you that a few years ago when I supported teacher testing while in my home state I was pretty well lambasted by the teachers association.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t believe we ought to be out there running down teachers and attacking them the way you did at the Republican convention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to be lifting them up and moving our children forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And let me just say that budget that you passed that I vetoed would have cut 50,000 kids out of Headstart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It would have eliminated the AmeriCorps plan and it would have cut back on student loans and scholarships.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, it would have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s a fact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s one of the big reasons I vetoed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to be doing more in education, not less.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, the AmeriCorps program, I must say, if that’s one of your successes, I wouldn’t speak about it too loudly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It costs about $27,000 to pay people to volunteer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got four million young people volunteering every year, the number hasn’t gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And you pick out 20,000, whether they need the money or not, and they get paid for volunteering.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I like young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I like teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m a product of a public school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You attended a private school for some time in your life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I like teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re not for school choice, you can’t be for school choice, because this is that special interest money again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When you get 99.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 5 percent of the money, we don’t know what happened to the other .

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 5 percent, we’re looking for it, somebody got it, but it all went to Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And this is part of that liberal establishment, one of those liberal things that you just can’t do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re for school uniforms and curfews and you’re opposed to truancy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now that’s not reform, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Why can’t Landale Shakespeare in Cleveland or Pilar Gonzales in Milwaukee give their children an opportunity to go to a better school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Some schools aren’t safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Some schools aren’t even safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Your choice is nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s give them a real choice, the kind of choice you had, and the kind of choice a lot of people have in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If we want to stop crime and teenage pregnancy, let’s start with education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, Senator Dole, let’s set the record straight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was able for two years when I was in, a very young boy to go to a Catholic school, but I basically went to public schools all my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve worked hard for a long time to make them better, 90 percent of our kids are there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You, it’s amazing to me, you are all for having more responsibility at the local level for everything except schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Where we don’t have very much money at the Federal level to spend on education, we ought to spend it helping the 90 percent of the kids that we can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If a local school district in Cleveland or anyplace else wants to have a private choice plan like Milwaukee did, let them have at it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I might say the results are highly ambiguous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I want to get out there and give a better education opportunity to all of our children and that’s why I vetoed the budget you passed with $30 billion in education cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was wrong, and my plan for the future is better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I had precisely in mind a lot of the people that were in the White House and other agencies who’ve never been had any experience, who came to Washington without any experience, they all were very liberal, of course, or they wouldn’t be in the administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And their idea was that they knew what was best for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, I feel very strongly about a lot of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I feel strongly about education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to help young people have an education, just as I had an education after World War II with the GI bill of Rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had millions of young men and women in subsequent subsequent wars change the face of the nation because the government helped with their education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now the reason they don’t have, The reason the President can’t support this is pretty obvious.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s not taking anything away from schools, it’s new money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s not being taken away from anybody else, except we’ll downsize the Department of Education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But this is a very liberal administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is an administration that gave you the big tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This administration tried to take over healthcare and impose a governmental system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is the administration that fought regulatory reform that is putting a lot of small businessmen and small businesswomen out of business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is the administration that fought the balanced budget amendment and vetoed a balanced budget and vetoed welfare reform twice, and the list goes on and on and on, that’s what I had in mind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want people in my administration and will have people in my administration who understand America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There won’t be 10 millionaires and 14 lawyers in the cabinet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There will be people with experience and people who understand America and people who’ve made it and know the hard knocks in life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When Senator Dole made that remark about all the elitists, all the young elitists in the administration, one of the young men who works for me who grew up in a house trailer looked at me and said, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: President, I know how you grew up, who is he talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you know this liberal charge, that’s what their party always drags out when they get in a tight race.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s sort of their golden oldie, you know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s a record they think they can play that everybody loves to hear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I just don’t think that dog will hunt this time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The American people should make up their own mind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Here’s the record: We cut deficit four years in a row for the first time before the Civil War — I mean, before World War II, and maybe before the Civil War, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got ten and a half million new jobs; we’ve got record numbers of those new small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve made every one of them eligible for a tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got declining crime rates, two million fewer people on welfare rolls before welfare reform passed, and a 50 percent increase in child support and a crime bill with 60 death penalties and 100,000 police and the assault weapons ban.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The American people can make up their mind about whether that’s a liberal record or a record that’s good for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Liberal, conservative, you put whatever label you want on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think it’s pretty liberal, I’ll put that label on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You take a look at all the programs you’ve advocated, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank goodness we had a Republican Congress there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The first thing you did when you came into office was set up the stimulus package, said we’ve got a little pork we want to scatter around America, $16 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And even some in your own party couldn’t buy that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I remember talking by the telephone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m not even certain you were too excited about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I won’t, I never repeat what I’ve talked to the President about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In any event, we saved the taxpayers $16 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And then came some other program, and then came healthcare, and then came the tax increase and a lot of these things stopped in 1994 because then the Congress changed, and I think we’ve done a good job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe that the purpose of politics is to give people the tools to make the most of their own lives; to reinforce the values of opportunity and responsibility, and to build a sense of community so we’re all working together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe in discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe you can protect the environment and grow the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe that we have to do these things with a government that’s smaller and less bureaucratic, but that we have to do them nonetheless.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s inconvenient for Senator Dole, but the truth is I’ve reduced the size of government more than my Republican predecessors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I did stop them, I admit that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I sure stopped their budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their budget cut enforcement for the Environmental Protection Agency by a third.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It cut funds to clean up toxic waste dumps with 10 million of our kids still living within four miles of a toxic waste dump, by a third.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It ended the principle that the polluters should pay for those toxic waste dumps unless it was very recent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their budget weakened our support for education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: $30 billion, even cut funds for scholarships and college loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their budget cut $270 billion in Medicare and, finally, their budget withdrew the national guarantee of healthcare to poor children, families with children with handicaps, the elderly in nursing homes, poor pregnant women.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was wrong for the country and calling it conservative won’t make it right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was a bad decision for America and would have been bad for our future if I hadn’t stopped it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, the President can define himself in any way he wants, but I think we have to look at the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Go back to the time he was, what, Texas director for George McGovern.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: George McGovern is a friend of mine, so I don’t mean, but he was a liberal, proud liberal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve just finished reading a book, I think it’s called — what is it called, what is it, The Demise of the Democratic Party by Ronald Cardash or something talking about all the liberal influences in the administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Whether it’s organized labor or whether it’s the Hollywood elite or whether some of the media elite or whether it’s the labor unions or whatever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And so I think you take a look at it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The bottom line is this: I think the American people, thought he’d recite all these bills and all these things, they want to know what’s going to happen to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’ve all got a lot of anxieties out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Did anybody complain when you raised taxes?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Did anybody go out and ask the people, how are you going to pay the extra money?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we want an economic package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We want the government to pinch their pennies for a change instead of the people pinching their pennies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s what our message is to the people watching.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Not all this back and forth, you voted this way, you voted that way, we want a better America as we go into the next century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The way you get a better America is to balance the budget and protect Medicare, Medicaid, education and the environment; to give a targeted tax cut — and let me talk about the education tax cut — to let people have a $10,000 deduction for the cost of college tuition in any year, any kind of college tuition; to give families a tax credit, a dollar for dollar reduction in their taxes for the cost of a typical community college so we can open that to everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And then to let people save in an IRA and withdraw from it without a tax penalty for education, home buying or medical expenses, that’s the right way to go into the 21st Century, balance the budget and cut taxes, not balloon with this $550 billion tax scheme.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let me say first, on the President’s promise for another tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean, I’ve told people as I’ve traveled around, all of you that got the tax cut he promised last time, vote for him in ’96 and not many hands go up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So the question is, would you buy a used election promise from my opponent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The people want economic reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re having a hard time making ends meet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got one parent working for the government, the other parent working for the family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is important business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is about getting the economy moving again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is about American jobs and opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about the government, as I said before, pinching its pennies for a change instead of the poor taxpayer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When they raise your taxes nobody runs around asking people where are you going to get the extra money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think the government can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Are there personal differences?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, my blood pressure is lower, my weight, my cholesterol, but I will not make health an issue in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I think he’s a bit taller than I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I think there are personal differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean, I’m not I don’t like to get into personal matters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: As far as I’m concerned, this is a campaign about issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about my vision for America and about his liberal vision for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And not about personal things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, I think his liberal vision is a thing of the past.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know he wants to disown it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t want to be a liberal either, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, but you’re stuck with it because that’s your record, that’s your record in Arkansas: The biggest tax increase in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The biggest crime increase in history, the biggest drug increase in history in Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, just for the record, when I was governor we had the lowest — second lowest tax burden of any state in the country, the highest job growth rate of any state when I ran for president and were widely recognized for a lot of other advances.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the important thing is, what are we going to do now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think a targeted tax cut is better for our future, targeted to education and child rearing, with the rest of the education plan, hooking up all of our classrooms to the Internet by the year 2000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Making sure we’ve got an army of reading volunteers, trained people to teach with parents and teachers so that our eight year olds can learn to read.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Investing in our environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Cleaning up two-thirds of the worst toxic waste dumps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Those plans are better than this $550 billion tax scheme.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, remember, folks, even Senator Dole’s campaign co-chair here, Senator D’Amato, says he’s got to cut Medicare to pay for this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Everybody who’s looked at it, 500 economists, seven Nobel prize winners, say it’s bad for the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to blow a hole in the deficit It’s going to raise taxes on nine million people and require bigger cuts than the one I vetoed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our plan is better, it will take us into the future with a growing economy and healthier families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m really encouraged to know of your renewed friendship with Al D’Amato, and I know he appreciates it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You didn’t even have tax cuts in your budget, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, the first two years you were president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It wasn’t until we had a Republican Congress you even thought about, you talked about tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Getting back to personal differences, I think, Jim, if you are a little more specific, but I think the President could clarify one thing tonight and that’s the question of pardons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know you talked about it on the Jim, with Jim Lehrer on the PBS show.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve never discussed Whitewater, as I’ve told you personally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m not discussing Whitewater now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I am discussing the power the President has to grant pardons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And hopefully in the next segment you could lay that to rest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, you know, he made that remark about Senator D’Amato.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He’s arranged for me to spend a lot more time with Senator D’Amato in the last couple years so I’m more familiar with his comments than I used to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say what I’ve said already about this pardon issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is an issue they’ve brought up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s under, there’s been no consideration of it, no discussion of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will tell you this: I will not give anyone special treatment and I will strictly adhere to the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that is what every president has done, as far as I know, in the past but what every other president’s has done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is something I take seriously and that’s my position.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it seems to me the president shouldn’t have any comment at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Particularly where it’s someone where you’ve had business dealings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you may be sending a signal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know, I’m not questioning anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But as a President of the United States, when somebody asks you about pardons, you say no comment, period.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think he made a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think when you make a mistake, you say I made a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But apparently his position hasn’t changed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If there are other specific areas, but beyond that I haven’t gotten into any of these things, as the President knows.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had that discussion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And again I know Senator D’Amato I think may have had a hearing or two on Whitewater, I can’t remember, but he’s not my general chairman, he’s a friend of mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And so is Senator Kennedy a friend of yours.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You bet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I remember one day on the floor I said now, gentlemen, let me tax your memories, and Kennedy jumped up and said, why haven’t we thought of that before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, so one of your liberal friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No comment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What’s the subject matter?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: See, if I say anything it’s going to be misconstrued.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think there is even a race between the two, it’s about our vision for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I happen to like President Clinton personally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m addressing him all evening as Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I said in 1992 he didn’t extend that courtesy to President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I respect the presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve served under a number of presidents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They all have their strengths and they all have their weaknesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I’d rather talk about my strengths.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think I have my strengths and I think the best thing going for Bob Dole is that Bob Dole keeps his word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a question between trust and fear, and I would say, I think, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, about all you’ve got going in this campaign is fear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re spending millions and millions of dollars in negative ads frightening senior citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know this to be a fact because I had one tell me last week, Senator don’t cut my Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m trying to save your Medicare, just as I rescued Social Security with a bipartisan commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have relatives on Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I used to sign welfare checks for my grandparents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know all about poverty and all about need and all about taking care of people, and that’s been my career in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll keep my word on the economic package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If I couldn’t cut taxes and balance the budget the same time, I wouldn’t look at you in the eye in your living room or wherever you might be and say that this is good for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: People will tell you who served with Bob Dole, agree or disagree, he kept his word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s what this race is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like the American people to know that I have worked very hard to be on their side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And to move this country forward and we’re better off than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the most important thing is my plan for the 21st Century is a better plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A targeted tax cut, a real commitment to educational reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A deep commitment to making welfare reform work with incentives to the private sector to move people from welfare to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now we have to create those jobs, now that we’re requiring people to go do work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A commitment to continuing step-by-step healthcare reform with the next step helping people who are between jobs to access healthcare and not lose it just because they are out of work for a while.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A commitment to grow the economy while protecting the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’d like them to know about me; that I’ve gotten up every day and worked for the American people and worked so that their children could have their dreams come true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I believe we’ve got the results to show we’re on the right track.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The most important thing is, I believe we’ve got the right ideas for the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I like, I like Senator Dole, you can probably tell we like each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just see the world in different ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you folks out there are going to have to choose who you think is right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’d say the first homeless bill in the Senate was the Dole-Byrd Byrd-Dole bill, I can’t remember who was in control then.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I remember working with Senator Ribicoff from Connecticut on the Hospice program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We now have 2500 hospices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: As I said, I’ve worked all my life when I was in the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I left on June 11th because I wanted the American people to know that I was willing to give up something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President Clinton ran for governor in 1990 and said he’s going to fill out his term, but he didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He’s president so I guess it’s a little better deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I wanted the American people to know I was willing to give up something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I wasn’t just getting more power and more power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I rolled the dice, I put my career on the line because I really believe the future of America is on the line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We can give you all these numbers, they don’t mean a thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you are out of work, you have nothing to eat or you can’t have medical care, or you’re holding a crack baby in your arms right now, what do you do next?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, America’s best days are ahead of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve seen the tough times, I know they can be better and I’ll lead America to a brighter future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s look at that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I ran for president, I said we’d cut the deficit in half in four years; we cut it by 60 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I said that our economic plan would produce eight million jobs, we have ten and a half million new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re number one in autos again, record numbers of new small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I said we’d put, pass a crime bill that would put 100,000 police on the street, ban assault weapons, and deal with the problems that ought to be dealt with with capital punishment, including capital punishment for drug kingpins, and we did that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I said we would change the way welfare works, and even before the bill passed we’d moved nearly two million people from welfare to work, working with states and communities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I said we’d get tougher with child support and child support enforcement’s up 50 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I said that I would work for tax relief for middle class Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The deficit was bigger than I thought it was going to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think they’re better off, all of us are, that we got the interest rates down and the deficit down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Republicans talk about it, but we’re the first the first administration in anybody’s lifetime looking at this program to bring that deficit down four years in a row.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We still gave tax cuts to 15 million working Americans, and now I’ve got a plan that’s been out there for two years, it could have been passed already, but instead the Republicans shut the government down to try to force their budget and their plan on me, and I couldn’t take that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we’ll get the rest of that tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so I think when you look at those results, you know the plan I’ve laid out for the future has a very good chance of being enacted if you’ll give me a chance to build that bridge to the 21st Century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, there he goes again, that line has been used before, I mean, exaggerating all the things that he did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t do all these things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let’s take all these four years in a row.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He came in with a high growth rate, the 1990 budget agreement, which some, you know, didn’t like, had some very tough cost controls, put a lot of pressure on Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The S & L crisis was over, they’re starting to sell assets, all that money was coming in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And he cut defense an extra $60 billion, threw a lot of people out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He talks about a smaller government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are actually more people in government except for people in defense related jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re gone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The government’s bigger than it was when President Kennedy was around, even though he says it’s not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In addition, Republican Congress cut $53 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So let’s just, let’s give credit where credit is due.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Governor Engler of Michigan cut taxes 21 times, created a lot of new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So did Governor Thompson, so did Governor Rowland.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: A lot of people ought to deserve credit, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When I’m President of the United States we’re going to have a governors’ council and we’re going to work directly with the governors to get power back to the people and back to the states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think a lot of people deserve credit and I’ve tried to give it to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I believe that my plan is better than Senator Dole’s ill-advised $550 billion scheme which I’ll say again will blow a hole in the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our plan will balance the budget, grow the economy, preserve the environment, and invest in education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have the right approach for the future and looks at the results.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is not midnight in America, Senator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We are better off than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, first, Jim, let me thank you and thank you, Senator Dole, and thank you, ladies and gentlemen, all of you listening tonight for the chance you’ve given us to appear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to say in the beginning that I am profoundly grateful for the chance that you have given me to serve as president for the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I never could have dreamed anything like this would come my way in life, and I’ve done my best to be faithful to the charge you’ve given me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud of the fact that America is stronger and more prosperous and more secure than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’m glad we’re going in the right direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve done my best tonight to lay out my plans for going forward to an even better future in the next century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to leave you with the thought that the things I do as president are basically driven by the people whose lives I have seen affected by what does or doesn’t happen in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The auto worker in Toledo who was unemployed when I was elected and now has a great job because we’re number one in auto production again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: All the people I’ve met who used to be on welfare who are now working and raising their children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think what others could do for our country and themselves if we did the welfare reform thing in the proper way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think of the man who grabbed me by the shoulder once with tears in his eyes and said his daughter was dying of cancer and he thanked me for giving him a chance to spend some time with her without losing his job because of the Family and Medical Leave Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think of all the people I grew up with and went to school with and who I stay in touch with and who nerve let me forget how what we do in Washington affects all of you out there in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Folks, we can build that bridge to the 21st Century, big enough and strong enough for all of us to walk across, and I hope you will help me build it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim; thank you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President; thank everyone for watching and listening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to address my remarks to the young people of America, because they’re the ones that are going to spend most of their life in the 21st Century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re the ones who have the challenges and they are people out there making predictions that it’s not going to be the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re not going to have the opportunities; there are going to be more deficits, more drugs, more crime, and less confidence in the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what you’re faced with, the parents are faced with, and the grand parents are faced with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s important, it’s their future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I would say to those I know there are more young people experimenting with drugs today than ever before; drug use has gone up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And if you care about the future of America, if you care about your future, just don’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I know that I’m someone older than you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I’ve had my anxious moments in my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve learned to feed myself and to walk and to dress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m standing here as proof that in America the possibilities are unlimited.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know who I am, and I know where I’m from, and I know where I want to take America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We are the greatest country on the face of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We do more good things for more people in our communities, our neighborhoods, than anywhere that I know of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is important business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This election is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I ask for your support, I ask for your help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And if you really want to get involved, just tap into my home page, www.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: God bless America.
